a3661.speech: "This gesture underlines the principle of collective support that unites our continent. We hope that this contribution will bring significant relief to the affected communities."

a3661.speaker: Ana Nembe, head of the African Union delegation
a3661.speech: "The AU's support is not limited to crisis response. It encompasses key areas such as development, peace and regional integration."

a3661.speaker: Gabriel H. Salee, Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
a3661.speech: Expressed the gratitude of the Liberian government: "On behalf of His Excellency President Joseph Nyuma Boakai and the Liberian people, I thank the African Union for this generous act. We commit to using these funds transparently so that they directly benefit the victims," ; also issued an appeal to other regional and international partners to support the reconstruction efforts.

a3702.speaker: Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Authority, in partnership with USAID and Feed the Future Ethiopia Value Chain (FTFE-VCA)
a3702.speech: Announced that the Cup of Excellence (COE) will be held in Ethiopia for the first time in March 2020, and that the COE will highlight Ethiopian coffee and stimulate new market opportunities for smallholder producers in the country.

a3961.speaker: John F. Kennedy Memorial Medical Center (Internal Memo to Patients dated July 24, 2025)
a3961.speech: "Subject: Updated pricelist for Caesarean section at Maternity. Dear All, Please be informed that effective August 1, 2025, the new price structure for C-Section are as stated below: Admission fees – $25 (1-5 days), Caesarean section – $90, Intra-Op meds & medical supplies -$65, Routine labs – $20, All other services will be billed as ordered" ; urged that all patients must make a deposit of the highlighted bills prior to SURGERY, and that receipts must be in the charts before taking the patient to the Theater/Ward.

a3961.speaker: Nyonblee Kangar-Lawrence, Liberian Senate Pro-Tempore (official Facebook post)
a3961.speech: Said that they are making an intervention to address the situation: "We have started to intervene in this. No woman in labor pain should have to pay a deposit before admission at any Government hospital in Liberia. Services should be provided immediately upon arrival. Delivery is an emergency."

a3961.speaker: Cllr. Taiwan Saye Gongloe, Liberian human rights lawyer
a3961.speech: Termed the situation as alarming and worrisome, while urging that Liberia takes charge of its health delivery sector, in order to avoid such a situation.

a3961.speaker: Cllr. Taiwan Saye Gongloe, Liberian human rights lawyer
a3961.speech: Accused Senator Kangar-Lawrence of public financial waste, thereby depriving Liberians of better healthcare, good roads, and better education due to the high financial budget and assistance her office continues to receive: "President Pro-Tempore Nyonblee Kangar-Lawrence makes about twenty-one thousand United States dollars a month. Last year, her salary was $254,000, plus benefits. On the other hand, the President Pro-Tempore of the United States made one hundred and ninety-three thousand United States dollars. I want the senate Pro-temp to lead the process and say no senator and representative will make more than two thousand United States dollar and government should not buy any lawmakers vehicle because with that we will be able to address the health, road and security challenge the country is facing because we will be cutting down public financial waste" ; termed Senator Lawrence's intervention in the JFK matter as complete hypocrisy, adding that the best way to express her concern is to propose a salary deduction for lawmakers and a reduction in their benefits.

a3961.speaker: Cllr. Taiwan Saye Gongloe, Liberian human rights lawyer
a3961.speech: Commenting on the justification of USAID withdrawing support from Liberia's health sector, which led to the increase in the fees, he argued that Liberia can't continue to depend on other people's taxpayers' money forever, while recommending policy and budgetary reform: "Listen to me, these are the same things that led this country to war. The spending by just 1% is so high that it's difficult for 99% to survive. In such a country, there is no possibility for peace and stability because people are angry. Whenever you develop an angry nation, you give rise to an uprising. JFK and government hospitals should be free for pregnant women, children, and old people. See the cars those people are riding. So, her call is not sincere."

a4115.speaker: Tuliameni Kalomoh, Namibian diplomat
a4115.speech: told New Era the US presidential transition will herald a dramatic change in tone and style given Biden and Trump’s diametrically different personalities and different worldviews ; “Biden will likely be more respectful towards the African continent and the African people, considering he won both the primaries and national presidential election in no small measure because of the African/Americans and other minority voters” ; “Trump was condescending and totally disdainful towards Africa and the African people. He called the continent and its people pejorative and derogatory names. His attitudes towards Africans border on racism. I doubt there are any sane African leaders and people who will miss Mr. Trump. I for one will certainly not.”

a4115.speaker: Tuliameni Kalomoh, Namibian diplomat
a4115.speech: was quick to add the continent will have to balance its expectations of the Biden administration with the prevailing realities: “The new administration, like the outgoing one will continue to pay some attention to the security issues in Somalia and broader Horn of African; Central African Republic; the Sahel region and the Lake Chad Basin countries to support the different countries in their respective fight against the scourge of terrorism and extremists” ; he said it should be noted that foreign policy, including African issues, received only scant, if any, attention by either Biden or Trump during the election campaign ; “The Covid-19 pandemic has so ravaged the economy of the US that I don’t see the US being able to provide economic assistance to Africa” ; Kalomoh believes Biden will renew the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) and continue to support Namibia through the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (Pepfar).

a4115.speaker: Kaire Mbuende, veteran diplomat
a4115.speech: said the Biden administration could return to an era where Africa will enjoy greater attention in US foreign policy and development cooperation ; “Biden administration commitment to multilateralism is a welcome development as Africa will engage the US in multilateral fora on a number of issues such as trade and development, reform of WTO (World Trade Organisation) and climate change” ; “As you may know, the Trump administration withdrew from the Paris Agreement. The excitement about the change of guard in Washington and the need to engage the US on the side of some Africa’s strategic partners such as the EU may divert their attention from Africa and prioritise their engagement with the US. Africa will not miss the Trump administration.”

a4404.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a4404.speech: Declared that South Africa would not be bullied by Donald Trump or anyone else in sovereign pursuit of its domestic and international policies: "We will not be deterred. We are a resilient people. We will not be bullied. We will stand together as a united nation." ; conceded that the funding freeze by the US, initially temporary but now permanent, had put the treatment of thousands of people in HIV programmes at risk, as well as the target of extending treatment to 1.1 million more.

a4404.speaker: Umamah Bakharia (Mail & Guardian reporting)
a4404.speech: According to Umamah Bakharia's reporting this week, thousands of people living with HIV and related ailments like TB have been handed a practical death sentence because Trump is annoyed about the Expropriation Act and South Africa's support for Palestine.

a4404.speaker: Aaron Motsoaledi, Health Minister of South Africa
a4404.speech: Told reporters this month that some 15 000 people employed in the health sector, including government workers and those whose organisations relied on US funding through Pepfar, stand to lose their jobs in the fallout.

a4421.speaker: U.S. media (reports)
a4421.speech: Reported that a federal judge in that country has ordered the Trump administration to temporarily lift its freeze on U.S. humanitarian and development funding, which had halted aid operations globally.

a4421.speaker: U.S. federal judge (ruling)
a4421.speech: The ruling, issued late Thursday, stated the financial devastation caused by the sudden cutoff of payments to suppliers and nonprofits executing U.S. aid programmes overseas; the administration now has five days to demonstrate compliance with the order.

a4421.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Namibia (non-response)
a4421.speech: Has yet to respond to enquiries regarding how this funding freeze affected USAID operations, including potential job losses or programmes disruptions there.

a4421.speaker: Another U.S. judge (ruling)
a4421.speech: Ruled against an executive order seeking to end birthright citizenship for children of undocumented immigrants.

a4601.speaker: Olivier Daipo, deputy chief of staff to the Minister of Trade and Industry; Lamarane Barri, deputy chief of staff to the Minister of Women, Family and Children; and Soumah Deli, technical adviser to the Minister of Finance and Budget
a4601.speech: Assured the companies of the committed institutional backing of their various ministerial departments, and called for a mobilisation of the private sector in all its components (an appeal launched together with Koffi Christophe, technical adviser to the Minister of National Education and Literacy, and Ando Tania, technical adviser to the Minister of National Cohesion and Solidarity).

a4601.speaker: Sonia Shahrigian, Country Director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) in Côte d'Ivoire
a4601.speech: Reiterated the commitment of the American government alongside Côte d'Ivoire some eight months from the end of the Compact programme; welcomed the good collaboration with the Ivorian side, particularly in strengthening the gender dimension in the education system, out of which the B4Gender initiative emerged; and called for this model of collaboration to be made lasting, expressing her deep conviction that the Ivorian private sector is capable of doing so in partnership with the public sector.

a4601.speaker: Mariam Fadiga Fofana, Executive Secretary of the CCESP
a4601.speech: Underlined the quality of the partnership model proposed by the B4Gender initiative: “The B4Gender initiative is thus the perfect example of the model we are striving to co-create, because it brings together three essential criteria. First, it is based on the Sustainable Development Goals, in this case SDGs 4 and 5 dedicated to quality education and gender-sensitive policies. Second, it aligns with the Government's priorities relating to Education and to the Gender Policy of the Ministry of National Education and Literacy, drawn up with the support of the Millennium Challenge Corporation. Third, it has the advantage of promoting partnerships between NGOs and companies with a view to generating measurable and lasting social impact.”

a4747.speaker: A leading civil society advocate (anonymous)
a4747.speech: “This is not just about the compact; it’s about restoring faith in our ability to deliver on our promises.”

a4849.speaker: Bill Gates, Chair of the Gates Foundation
a4849.speech: Speaking at the 2025 Goalkeepers event, said the $912 million pledge to the Global Fund aims to shore up lifesaving health initiatives at a time when global health funding has fallen to its lowest level in 15 years ; said low global funding is threatening decades of progress in reducing child mortality ; described the situation as a crossroads for the world and urged renewed commitment to saving children's lives and eradicating preventable diseases ; warned that millions of children's lives are at stake, stressing that global leaders have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to reverse the decline: "Humanity is at a crossroads. With millions of children's lives on the line, global leaders have a once-in-a-generation chance to do something extraordinary" ; "The choices they make now—whether to go forward with proposed steep cuts to health aid or to give the world's children the chance they deserve to live a healthy life—will determine what kind of future we leave for the next generation."

a4849.speaker: Bill Gates, Chair of the Gates Foundation
a4849.speech: Warned that the current decline threatens to reverse past progress, but said he remained optimistic that governments could still make the right choices to save lives: "What is happening to the health of the world's children is worse than most people realise, but our long-term prospects are better than most people can imagine" ; "I don't expect most governments to suddenly restore foreign aid to historic levels, but I believe governments can and will do what's needed to save as many children as possible."

a4849.speaker: Bill Gates, Chair of the Gates Foundation
a4849.speech: Noted that every dollar invested in the Global Fund delivers an estimated $19 in health and economic returns.

a4849.speaker: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) study
a4849.speech: Revealed that global development assistance for health (DAH) fell by 21 per cent between 2024 and 2025, pushing funding to its lowest point since 2010.

a4849.speaker: Gates Foundation and IHME (findings)
a4849.speech: Suggest that sustaining global investments in child health and scaling innovations could cut child mortality in half again over the next 20 years.

a4849.speaker: Gates Foundation (organisational statement)
a4849.speech: Announced a $912 million pledge to the Global Fund to fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria, bringing its total contribution to the Global Fund to $4.9 billion ; said it will also release its 2025 Goalkeepers Report, which will focus on the impact of leaders' decisions between now and year-end on the survival of children worldwide.

a4849.speaker: Bill Gates, Chair of the Gates Foundation
a4849.speech: Announced earlier this year that he would donate virtually all of his wealth to the foundation, with plans to spend $200 billion over the next 20 years before winding down its operations, targeting three priorities: ending preventable deaths of mothers and babies, eradicating infectious diseases, and lifting millions out of poverty.

a4871.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance Minister
a4871.speech: Remarking at the signing ceremony, said the agreement marks another step in the historic bilateral relationship between Liberia and the United States; highlighted their commitment to addressing pressing development challenges; expressed optimism about future collaborative efforts and reaffirmed the necessity of such partnerships as Liberia navigates significant developmental obstacles; "The Government of the United States, through the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), has proven to be a steadfast and reliable partner." ; "We are excited to be signing this agreement today." ; expressed gratitude to the teams that have worked diligently to secure increased support for Liberia, acknowledged the profound impact these agreements will have on the lives of the Liberian people, and emphasized the government's commitment to further collaborations that will improve the nation's welfare.

a4871.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance Minister (MFDP Boss)
a4871.speech: Said the investments outlined in the agreement are designed to drive inclusive economic growth, create jobs, promote effective governance, and facilitate essential services across the nation ; revealed that the health sector will receive particular attention, with 55 ongoing projects aimed at supporting Liberia's health policy and enhancing essential health services.

a4871.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance Minister
a4871.speech: Emphasized the importance of a sustainable development approach, highlighting the need for investments in the domestic economy that can generate employment opportunities, especially in the private sector ; noted that accountability and transparency in public sector institutions are critical for ensuring resources effectively benefit the populace.

a4871.speaker: Mark C. Toner, US Ambassador accredited to Liberia
a4871.speech: Disclosed that the agreement established between the U.S. government and the Government of Liberia underscores a mutual commitment to advancing the country's development; emphasized the importance of this agreement, which adds to a broader $640 million five-year development objective launched in May 2020; "This funding is more than just financial support; it embodies our unwavering commitment to Liberia's future." ; "Today, we celebrate not only an addition to our financial contributions but also the shared values that unite our nations." ; continued that the allocated funds aim to bolster the Liberian government's initiatives in essential sectors such as health, education, and inclusive economic growth, with specific plans including training teachers, delivering health commodities to communities, and expanding economic opportunities within the agriculture sector.

a4871.speaker: Mark C. Toner, US Ambassador accredited to Liberia
a4871.speech: While expressing hope for the future, acknowledged the challenges, including corruption and capacity constraints; "Together, we must reinforce the necessary structures to confront these challenges," he urged ; "Together, we are laying the groundwork for a brighter future - one that fosters hope, opportunity, and growth in Liberia."

a4871.speaker: Government of Liberia and the United States (joint account of the agreement)
a4871.speech: According to both countries, the amendment will see an additional US$114,488,125.00 added to the DOAG of 2020.

a5037.speaker: Financial Times
a5037.speech: Announced that the 12th edition of its flagship Africa Summit will take place in London on October 21-22, 2025, under the theme "Africa in a Changing World," bringing together African Heads of State, policymakers, CEOs, investors and next-generation entrepreneurs to explore the continent's place in an era of geopolitical upheaval, economic uncertainty and rapid technological change.

a5037.speaker: Financial Times (statement)
a5037.speech: "The dramatic changes to America's foreign policy in Donald Trump's second term and his upending of the decades-old global trading system present challenges, uncertainties and risks for Africa as other outside powers intervene." ; notes there may also be opportunities if Africa can pivot toward trade and investment over aid.

a5106.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5106.speech: Says the federal government is too bloated and too much money is lost to waste and fraud.

a5106.speaker: Congressional Democrats
a5106.speech: Say Trump is encroaching on the legislature's constitutional authority over federal spending, even as his fellow Republicans who control majorities in both chambers of Congress have largely supported the moves.

a5106.speaker: Sources (anonymous, told Reuters)
a5106.speech: The speed and breadth of Musk's effort has produced growing frustration among some of Trump's aides over a lack of coordination, including White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, sources told Reuters.

a5106.speaker: Sources familiar with the job cuts (anonymous, told Reuters)
a5106.speech: Almost half of the probationary workers at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and others at the National Institutes of Health are being forced out.

a5106.speaker: People familiar with the plans (anonymous)
a5106.speech: The U.S. Forest Service is firing around 3,400 recent hires, while the National Park Service is terminating about 1,000.

a5106.speaker: Two people familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a5106.speech: The tax-collecting Internal Revenue Service is preparing to fire thousands of workers next week, a move that could squeeze resources ahead of Americans' April 15 deadline to file income taxes.

a5106.speaker: Organizations impacted by the reductions
a5106.speech: According to them, federal programs have stopped hiring seasonal firefighters and halted removal of fire hazards such as dead wood from forests, a month after wildfires devastated Los Angeles.

a5106.speaker: Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary
a5106.speech: Shrugged off those concerns, comparing Musk's so-called Department of Government Efficiency to a financial audit. "These are serious people, and they're going from agency to agency, doing an audit, looking for best practices," he told Fox Business Network.

a5106.speaker: Budget experts
a5106.speech: Say Musk is relying on a coterie of young engineers with little government experience to manage his DOGE campaign, and their early cuts appear to be driven more by ideology than driving down costs.

a5106.speaker: Nick Gioia, army veteran and fired USDA Economic Research Service employee
a5106.speech: "I've done a lot for my country and as a veteran who served his country, I feel like I've been betrayed by my country" ; "I don't feel like this has anything to do with federal workers, I feel like this is just a game" ; "To sit here and watch people like Mr. Musk tweet out how he feels like he's doing a great job, he doesn't realize what he's doing to people's lives."

a5106.speaker: Steve Lenkart, executive director of the National Federation of Federal Employees union
a5106.speech: Said he expects Musk, whose SpaceX businesses has major contracts with the U.S. federal government, and the Trump administration to concentrate on agencies that regulate industry and finance. "That's really what this whole thing is really all about," Lenkart said. "It's getting government out of the way of industry and incredibly rich people, which is why Elon Musk is so excited about this."

a5106.speaker: Sources familiar with the matter (anonymous, told Reuters)
a5106.speech: About 1,200 to 2,000 workers at the Department of Energy were laid off, including 325 from the National Nuclear Security Administration, which oversees the nuclear stockpile; those layoffs have been "partly rescinded" to retain essential nuclear security workers, one of the sources said.

a5106.speaker: Court order issued on Friday
a5106.speech: According to the order, the administration has temporarily agreed not to fire any more staff at the U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, offering workers there an 11th-hour reprieve ahead of feared mass layoffs.

a5121.speaker: Prof. Ali Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare (represented by Dr. Nse Akpan, Director of Port Health Services)
a5121.speech: Said that in 2023 approximately 71,000 Nigerians succumbed to Tuberculosis (TB), with only one in four Nigerians having accurate knowledge about the disease; reaffirmed the Federal Government's commitment to eradicating tuberculosis despite facing significant funding challenges; emphasized that Nigeria is among the top 10 countries with the triple burden of TB, drug-resistant TB, and HIV-associated TB.

a5121.speaker: Dr. Walter Kazadi Mulombo, World Health Organization (WHO) Country Representative (represented by Dr Mya Ngon, Team Lead, Communicable & Non Communicable Diseases, WHO)
a5121.speech: In a goodwill message said Nigeria accounts for more than 5% of the global TB burden, with an estimated 499,000 TB cases occurring annually; hinted that despite the challenges Nigeria has made significant progress in its TB response efforts, with a 300% increase in TB notification from 138,583 in 2020 to 418,198 in 2024, and a case detection gap reduced from 73% in 2019 to 17% in 2024; emphasized the need for sustained efforts to end the TB epidemic, particularly in the face of emerging challenges such as Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB) and the high number of HIV cases ; urged everyone to join forces in solidarity, emphasizing that TB is curable and treatable, and encouraged anyone coughing for two weeks or more to go for a TB test at the nearest health facility: "Yes, we can end TB epidemic in Nigeria; We fit do am."

a5121.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a5121.speech: Has pledged its continued support to Nigeria in developing and implementing guidelines, plans, and strategic documents to end the TB epidemic.

a5121.speaker: Ms. Uzoma Nwofor, Senior Communications Manager, Institute of Human Virology Nigeria (IHVN)
a5121.speech: Said Nigeria's fight against tuberculosis has received a significant boost, with the Institute playing a pivotal role in expanding TB case detection: between 2021-2024, IHVN-supported facilities tested over 3.5 million individuals, leading to the detection and notification of more than 350,000 TB cases, contributing substantially to Nigeria's national case notification targets.

a5152.speaker: Government of Ethiopia
a5152.speech: Tuesday announced the launch of a new initiative dubbed “Ethio-Aid”, aiming to substitute the assistance being withheld by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID); it is a national disaster response mechanism intended to soften the blow caused by the aid cut and address emergencies using domestically mobilised resources.

a5152.speaker: Draft proclamation on disaster risk management (presented to parliament)
a5152.speech: According to the draft, 3 percent of the national budget will be allocated annually to a dedicated disaster response fund; the draft proclamation specifies that both governmental and non-governmental entities will be part of this national contribution effort.

a5152.speaker: Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission
a5152.speech: recently told legislators that the goal of Ethio-Aid is to enhance the country’s capacity to respond to natural disasters, conflict-related emergencies, and other crises, and that in addition to addressing domestic needs, the initiative is also intended to support neighbouring countries during times of hardship.

a5152.speaker: Officials from the Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission
a5152.speech: indicated that the funds collected will be used to build a permanent, well-resourced disaster response institution.

a5190.speaker: Fapgaz and Guinee Gaz (both parties to the case)
a5190.speech: As soon as the hearing opened, requested a postponement because of the absence of the defendant, Kaman Sadji Diallo.

a5190.speaker: Francis Kova Zoumanigui, president of the appeals chamber of the Court for the Repression of Economic and Financial Offences (CRIEF)
a5190.speech: Taking note of the request, postponed the hearing to 11 March 2025 for the opening of arguments.

a5190.speaker: Guinee Gaz (company, legal complaint)
a5190.speech: Had sued Fapgaz and its managing director, Kaman Sadji Diallo, for “unfair competition and abuse of authority infringing its import rights”; and lodged an appeal before the appeals chamber to challenge the judgment handed down on 23 December last.

a5190.speaker: CRIEF trial chamber presided over by Yacouba Conte (court ruling)
a5190.speech: Had dismissed Guinee Gaz's claim and acquitted Fapgaz and its managing director of the charges, holding that the offence was not made out, and ordered Guinee Gaz to pay one billion Guinean francs in damages to the defendants.

a5191.speaker: Cllr. Fanta Barclay, IP attorney and head judge of the competition
a5191.speech: Highlighted the quality displayed by each school in various categories, acknowledging their performances in IP project presentations, role play, and copyright, related rights, and trademark quizzes ; “We are all winners. The results reflect the strength of each school's performance across various categories, including the presentation of IP-related projects, role play, and a quiz on copyright and related rights, and trademark.”

a5191.speaker: Daniel O. Sando, Deputy Minister for Press and Public Affairs, Ministry of Information, Cultural Affairs, and Tourism
a5191.speech: Emphasized the importance of educating students on Intellectual Property to enhance their understanding of how it aligns with their creativity ; highlighted the significance of Liberia keeping up with evolving global trends, including the realm of IP ; acknowledged Liberia's previous lack of focus on intellectual property but commended the new leadership of LIPO for implementing programs to educate various sectors of Liberian society ; underlined the crucial role of starting with young people, particularly students who hold the key to shaping Liberia's future, and emphasized the need to integrate instructional modules on IP into the national curriculum, with continuous engagement and training of teachers ; suggested that as a member state of WIPO, Liberia could introduce similar programs in its school systems, citing WIPO's IP4Youth&Teachers initiative as a model.

a5191.speaker: Garmai Koboi, Director General of the Liberia Intellectual Property Office (LIPO)
a5191.speech: In her opening speech, noted that the initiative is not just a standalone event; it is a cornerstone of a broader vision championed by President Joseph Boakai's administration ; “The President firmly believes that the youth are the backbone of our nation and that empowering them with knowledge and resources is paramount for Liberia's sustainable development. Therefore, as we integrate intellectual property education into our schools, we are equipping our students with the tools they need to navigate and contribute to a global economy that increasingly values creativity and innovation” ; noted that under President Boakai's leadership LIPO is committed to fostering an environment where ideas can flourish and inventions can be protected ; “This competition is a reflection of that commitment. It is designed to cultivate a culture that recognizes the importance of intellectual property in economic growth, cultural development, and technological advancement” ; “To the teachers and mentors who have guided these students, we acknowledge your pivotal role. Your guidance has not only prepared them for this competition but has also instilled in them values that will last a lifetime. You are shaping the leaders, innovators, and visionaries of tomorrow” ; added that the competition is not the end of the project but the beginning of long-term initiatives ; “This commitment is the cornerstone of President Joseph Boakai's administration's efforts to build a nation where creativity is celebrated, protected, and transformed into tangible assets that drive progress.”

a5191.speaker: Garmai Koboi, Director General of the Liberia Intellectual Property Office (LIPO)
a5191.speech: Lauded WIPO and ARIPO for their unwavering support and commitment, which she said have been instrumental in making the initiative a reality ; “Your partnership signifies a shared vision for a future where intellectual property rights are respected and upheld, fueling innovation and progress across Africa and the world.”

a5208.speaker: Halifa Sallah, PDOIS Secretary General
a5208.speech: Informed media practitioners at a press conference that PDOIS will embark on a nationwide tour from the 20th to the 31st of October 2024, and said that during the tour the team will meet members, leaders of the party within regions as well as citizens of the country to engage them for a national conversation on the future of this country and what needs to be done to enable the Gambian people to take charge of their country.

a5208.speaker: Halifa Sallah, PDOIS Secretary General
a5208.speech: Said the Gambia cannot carry itself in the world from an economic point of view because it does not have the money to import goods; the reason, he said, is because it is not producing what it needs and what it can export. The economy of this country will only work if all the economic sectors are productive, he insisted.

a5208.speaker: Halifa Sallah, PDOIS Secretary General
a5208.speech: On the constitutional building process, he reminded that it is the people who are the makers of the Constitution and without one there cannot be a republic; the executive, he said, can only propose but the National Assembly can also dispose.

a5208.speaker: Halifa Sallah, PDOIS Secretary General
a5208.speech: Touched on the Russia-Ukraine and Israeli-Palestinian conflict as lack of world leadership to end it.

a5208.speaker: Halifa Sallah, PDOIS Secretary General
a5208.speech: On the media, he said journalists are expected to report in good faith and in the public interest; if, however, something is written not based on facts, it should be countered by producing the facts.

a5382.speaker: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), “common but differentiated responsibilities” principle
a5382.speech: requires developed countries to take the lead in providing financial assistance to developing countries for climate action.

a5418.speaker: Linda Thomas-Greenfield, US envoy (ambassador) to the UN
a5418.speech: Warned that Israel must immediately address the “catastrophic humanitarian situation” in Gaza, as the deadline approaches to improve the flow of aid or face cuts to American military assistance ; said the reports of children going days without food in Jabalia had made her think about how she had seen a girl die of starvation almost three decades ago ; said the Biden administration had made clear to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Israel must address the humanitarian crisis in Gaza immediately and that the US “rejects any Israeli efforts to starve Palestinians in Jabalia, or anywhere else” ; “The US has stated clearly that Israel must allow food, medicine and other supplies into all of Gaza – especially the north, and especially as winter sets in – and protect the workers distributing it.”

a5418.speaker: United Nations
a5418.speech: Says only 10% of that number (350 lorries daily) have crossed into Gaza each day on average since then.

a5418.speaker: Danny Danon, Israel’s ambassador to the UN
a5418.speech: Said Israel was going “above and beyond its humanitarian obligations” and blamed Hamas.

a5418.speaker: Danny Danon, Israel’s ambassador to the UN
a5418.speech: Rejected international criticism of the Israeli parliament’s decision to ban the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (Unrwa) from working in Israel.

a5418.speaker: Israel’s allies
a5418.speech: Have warned that Unrwa plays a critical role in delivering humanitarian assistance to Gaza, where it is the largest humanitarian organisation on the ground.

a5418.speaker: Tor Wennesland, UN Middle East peace envoy
a5418.speech: Said in a briefing to the UN Security Council in New York on Tuesday that he had witnessed a “horrific humanitarian nightmare” during a recent visit to Gaza ; said the north of the Palestinian territory had received virtually no humanitarian assistance since the start of October, when the Israeli military began a ground offensive in the Jabalia area.

a5418.speaker: Israeli military
a5418.speech: Said its ground offensive in the Jabalia area was aimed at stopping Hamas fighters from regrouping there.

a5448.speaker: Mohammed Ahmed Al Hammadi, Deputy Director of the Department of International Organizations at the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a5448.speech: Chaired the preparatory meeting and pleaded for “collective work” in accompanying Somalia towards peace and reconstruction, while insisting on the need for “joint solutions developed in coordination with international partners.”

a5448.speaker: Qatar
a5448.speech: Reaffirmed its commitment to structural support for Somalia, highlighting the importance of moving out of the cycle of emergency humanitarian aid in order to favour the financing of long-term development projects—an approach aimed at strengthening the Somali government's capacity to respond to the needs of its population and to consolidate national institutions.

a5563.speaker: Volker Turk, United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a5563.speech: Launched an urgent appeal during the 54th Session of the Human Rights Council for an international intervention to restore security in Haiti ; urged the international community to act decisively in the face of this crisis in Haiti, warning that time is running out and lives are at stake, and that the restoration of security, respect for human rights and the sustainable development of the Haitian nation depend on immediate and coordinated action by the global community.

a5563.speaker: Report of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights on Haiti
a5563.speech: Highlights the gravity of the situation in Haiti: since the beginning of 2023 more than 2,400 people killed, nearly 1,000 kidnapped and more than 900 injured in only eight months; gang brutality reaching shocking levels, with acts of mutilation and burning of bodies broadcast on social media; women and girls particularly vulnerable to gang violence, including gang rapes; gangs continuing to recruit children. The report stresses that to end the cycle of violence the Haitian state must hold accountable those responsible for crimes as well as its own officials in the police, the courts and the prison system; that strict control of public spending is essential to prevent corruption and that support for the judicial system is needed to investigate and prosecute those suspected of corruption; and it highlights the inhumane conditions in Haitian prisons, where more than 11,000 detainees are crammed into facilities designed for about a third of that number.

a5693.speaker: Cape Verdean government (press release)
a5693.speech: “This historic visit, which also highlights Cape Verde's growing credibility and influence on the world stage, comes following the successful reception by the Prime Minister of the US Secretary of State, Antony Blinken, earlier this year in the city of Praia, further consolidating Cape Verde's role as a strategic partner in the region,” reads the press release ; the same source emphasises that the visit serves as a testament to the strong and growing relationship between Cape Verde and the United States, highlighting Cape Verde as a model of stability, democracy and partnership in Africa and in the world ; according to the same source, this is the first visit by a sitting US President to Cape Verde and the first stop of Joe Biden's trip to the African continent.

a5786.speaker: Ntsokoane Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a5786.speech: His initial reaction [to the devastating US tariffs]? A light-hearted quip: “Trump is our fellow man.’’

a5786.speaker: Makotoko Moshe, Revolution for Prosperity legislator of Matsieng
a5786.speech: Asked why inmates are not dying in large numbers.

a5786.speaker: Dr Retšelisitsoe Matlanyane, Minister of Finance and Development Planning (2025/26 Budget Estimates)
a5786.speech: Confirmed the staggering figure that 760 000 young people are unemployed, in the 2025/26 Budget Estimates she presented.

a5850.speaker: Beatriz Grinsztejn, International Aids Society (IAS) president
a5850.speech: "Pepfar has been one of the greatest success stories in global health, transforming the HIV response," speaking at a press conference during the 13th IAS Conference in Kigali ; said global advocacy had played a key role in persuading US lawmakers to preserve the programme, "reminding them that decisions about Pepfar shape the health and futures of people around the world."

a5850.speaker: Beatriz Grinsztejn, International Aids Society (IAS) president
a5850.speech: Warned that uncertainty persists, with ongoing threats to global health funding, and urged continued vigilance from all parties involved.

a5850.speaker: Kenneth Ngure, IAS president-elect
a5850.speech: Underlined the importance of the decision for Africa: "Pepfar is a lifeline for communities across Africa. Restoring this funding would mean hope for people living with and affected by HIV. But African leadership must remain central in shaping our response and we need to continue advancing conversations around sustainable financing - including stronger domestic investments and strategies to reduce dependence on global donors."

a5850.speaker: International Aids Society (IAS)
a5850.speech: According to the IAS, Pepfar has saved 26 million lives over the past two decades and protecting the programme "could save millions more."

a5850.speaker: Maziko Matemba, Executive Director of the Health Rights Education Programme (Malawi)
a5850.speech: "Pepfar provides significant support, particularly in strengthening systems for the provision of HIV-related services." ; added that when the US government decided to freeze the support, many programmes in developing countries, especially those directly involved in HIV work, stalled.

a5850.speaker: Maziko Matemba, Executive Director of the Health Rights Education Programme (Malawi)
a5850.speech: "We need a smooth transition and for a country like Malawi, which has received support through Pepfar, this is crucial. A smooth transition will help ensure that in future, the country can absorb some of the programmes or services that Pepfar has been providing."

a5850.speaker: Executive Order 14169, 'Reevaluating and Realigning United States Foreign Aid' (signed by President Donald Trump, January 2025)
a5850.speech: Paused all US foreign development assistance programmes for 90 days to allow for a review, leading to the suspension of existing foreign aid initiatives including Pepfar, with exceptions made for "life-saving assistance."

a5953.speaker: President Barack Obama of the United States
a5953.speech: Has now apologised for the unfortunate and sad incident at the Kunduz hospital.

a5953.speaker: Carrie P. Snow, philosopher
a5953.speech: “When you think of the long and gloomy history of man, you will find that more hideous crime has been committed in the name of obedience than have ever been in the name of rebellion.”

a5953.speaker: President Muhammadu Buhari of Nigeria
a5953.speech: Presumed, in his address to USA lawmakers during his maiden state visit to Washington DC, that Western superpowers who fail to assist in providing weapons to rout Boko Haram are vicariously guilty of collusion with or are acquiescing with terrorists to kill and maim innocent Nigerians.

a5953.speaker: A Yazidi girl (15-year-old captive, interviewed by PBS NewsHour)
a5953.speech: “They brought everyone to a school, put the women upstairs, and drove the men away. I didn’t want to let my mother go, but they were pulling us from our mothers and beating us. The children were all put in cars. They said, ‘We’re going to sell you to others, and you will have sex with them.’” ; told how she and her siblings were captured, separated, and, for four months, she was shuttled between towns and cities hundreds of miles apart, even being sent to Syria.

a5953.speaker: Marcia Biggs, PBS NewsHour special correspondent (report ‘Freed And Not Freed’)
a5953.speech: Reported that in the months that followed the kidnap, a network of activists sprung up throughout Northern Iraq, an underground railroad of sorts, coordinating rescue efforts, and that their phone numbers quickly spread among captive girls, who used smuggled phones to call for help and give their location; stated that “At times, the Kurdish regional government has stepped in to grease the wheels,” and that KRG envoy Dr. Nouri Othman told her about two girls who escaped their captors in Raqqa and ran to a nearby house but were turned away by the owner, too scared to take the chance; reported that about 400 Yazidi women and girls are now free.

a5953.speaker: Dr. Nouri Othman, Envoy to Internally Displaced Persons, Kurdish Regional Government
a5953.speech: Said he called the house owner and pleaded with him to keep the two girls at his home for a couple of days, and that he had to promise to pay him: “Nobody is going to risk their life without getting something in return. You have to pay them.” ; revealed that “Some families are raising money to buy back their girls, racking up thousands of dollars in debt.”

a5953.speaker: Dr. Nouri Othman, Envoy to Internally Displaced Persons, Kurdish Regional Government
a5953.speech: On whether the government funds a programme to buy back the girls: “I’m not buying them, no. Maybe I’m paying some people. They are helping me get them back… The important thing is I want these people to be back. They are my responsibility.” ; told PBS that his government has spent over $1.5 million to rescue the girls, and on the ethical question responded: “Well, I’m not—not paying ISIS fighters. This is one. Second thing, these are Kurdish citizens. And I don’t care where the money goes personally. I care how to rescue the people.”

a5953.speaker: The Punch Newspaper of April 15
a5953.speech: Reported that 187 Chibok girls have been rescued.

a6339.speaker: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief) and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) (joint statement on the conference)
a6339.speech: The conference “aims to mobilise resources and coordinate efforts to provide essential assistance in order to deliver urgent aid to some 33 million people in need, including 11 million people who have been displaced, to save lives, protect civilians and promote efforts to help those affected emerge from the crisis.” ; It also aims to insist on the need for immediate humanitarian aid, the protection of civilians and support for initiatives targeting displaced people and refugees.

a6339.speaker: United Nations (estimates)
a6339.speech: The United Nations estimates at nearly 33 million the number of people in need of humanitarian aid and protection in the region, among them about 11 million internally displaced people and refugees in the Sahel and around Lake Chad.

a6685.speaker: PAICV (opposition party)
a6685.speech: Declared itself in favour of the fisheries agreement between Cabo Verde and the European Union, but argued that it must be accompanied by studies proving the sustainability of fishery resources and guaranteeing that there is no negative impact on the activities of national fishermen.

a6685.speaker: UCID (opposition party)
a6685.speech: Stated that the country could obtain greater benefits if measures were implemented to strengthen the national fleet.

a6685.speaker: MpD (governing party)
a6685.speech: Argued that the agreement is based on the principles of transparency, sustainability and equitable sharing of benefits.

a6685.speaker: Jose Filomeno Monteiro, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Cabo Verde
a6685.speech: Denied that the fisheries agreement with the EU harms Cabo Verde, explaining that the EEZ is not equivalent to territorial waters and that the passage of foreign vessels is permitted under international law ; stressed that the agreement covers migratory species and guarantees financial compensation for the fisheries sector and coastal communities.

a6685.speaker: Financial Times poll
a6685.speech: Revealed that 60% of Americans agreed with the freeze on American international aid under the direction of USAID, taken by Donald Trump and implemented by Elon Musk. Only 12% of those polled disagreed with the idea that significant amounts of aid funds are wasted on corruption and administrative costs, to the detriment of those truly in need.

a6685.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde
a6685.speech: Clarified today that Biosfera's claim about the sale of tuna caught in Cabo Verdean waters at "13 escudos per kilo" results from a simplified interpretation of the financial compensation under the Fisheries Agreement with the European Union; according to the Executive, that figure does not reflect the reality of the agreement, since it disregards additional fees paid by European vessel owners, as well as indirect investments in monitoring, sustainability and the development of the national fisheries sector.

a6685.speaker: President of the Association of Fishing Vessel Owners of Cabo Verde (Apesc)
a6685.speech: "The problem is not the fisheries agreement but rather its application in practice" ; considered that the problem does not lie in the fisheries agreement that the country has been renewing with the European Union, but rather in its practical application.

a6685.speaker: Jorge Santos, Minister of the Sea of Cabo Verde
a6685.speech: Said this Tuesday that the new fisheries agreement between Cabo Verde and the European Union, approved by the Fisheries Committee of the European Parliament, "was the agreement that was possible".

a6685.speaker: Abraao Vicente, Minister of the Sea of Cabo Verde
a6685.speech: Said the government intends to resume dialogue with vessel owners for the creation of an industrial fishing fleet, in reaction to the renewal of the new implementation protocol of the fisheries agreement with the European Union.

a6685.speaker: Carla Grijo, European Union Ambassador to Cabo Verde
a6685.speech: Said that Cabo Verde has demonstrated knowledge and effectiveness in implementing the fisheries agreement with the European Union, but that there is a communication deficit regarding the agreement in the archipelago, speaking on the sidelines of the joint meeting on the fisheries agreement in Sao Vicente.

a6685.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde (relevant ministry)
a6685.speech: Announced today that the European Union has approved a new temporary derogation from the preferential rules of origin for a period of three years, "but it will probably be the last", and guaranteed that the necessary investments in the fisheries sector are being made so that the archipelago can comply, within two and a half years, with the rules of origin approved by the European Commission.

a6685.speaker: Claudia Monteiro de Aguiar, Member of the European Parliament (PSD)
a6685.speech: Considered that the fisheries agreement between the European Union and Cabo Verde "results in important support" for the sector, but admitted that it could have been for a higher amount.

a6685.speaker: PAICV and UCID (opposition parties)
a6685.speech: State that the new fisheries agreement document has still not been made available, despite the request made, and that they know only what was presented by the Government.

a6685.speaker: President of the Association of Fishing Vessel Owners of Cabo Verde (APESC)
a6685.speech: Defended today, at a press conference held in Mindelo, that national vessel owners are giving the Government the benefit of the doubt regarding the new protocol of the fisheries agreement between Cabo Verde and the European Union.

a6685.speaker: Source from the environmental association Biosfera I
a6685.speech: Told Radio Morabeza that it prefers to remain silent on the new fisheries agreement between Cabo Verde and the EU; the same position was taken by the Movement Against Pollution in Cabo Verde.

a6685.speaker: Source from an environmental movement (anonymous)
a6685.speech: Told Lusa that the movement wants shark fishing to be banned from the agreement between Cabo Verde and the European Union, whose second round of negotiations for a new document is taking place this week.

a6739.speaker: Abdoulaye Sacca Bawa, director of the Bassila zone hospital
a6739.speech: He reports that major achievements have been made under the “Médecins sans vacances” initiative, including the acquisition of a steriliser, an incinerator and an oxygen concentrator; this equipment has made possible a significant reduction in the maternal and infant mortality rate and the effective care of women and other users.

a6739.speaker: Sandrine Platteau, Ambassador of Belgium to Benin
a6739.speech: made known that health is the basis of a country's development through good human capital. “The delegation is very impressed by the achievements made thanks to the MSV project in this hospital. The figures communicated in terms of the reduction of the maternal and infant mortality rate are close to our hearts, because these two factors remain a challenge in Benin,” the diplomat recalled.

a6777.speaker: Court filing, U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia
a6777.speech: Showed late on Thursday that a federal judge ordered the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump to restore funding for hundreds of foreign aid contractors, temporarily blocking the administration from canceling foreign aid contracts and awards that were in place before Trump took office on January 20 - the first such ruling to reverse Trump's funding freeze on foreign assistance.

a6777.speaker: Hundreds of foreign aid contractors (plaintiffs, including two health organizations that receive U.S. funding for overseas programs)
a6777.speech: Argued that they were negatively impacted by the 90-day blanket freeze on foreign aid.

a6777.speaker: Amir Ali, U.S. District Judge
a6777.speech: Wrote in a filing that the stated purpose in suspending all foreign aid was to provide the opportunity to review programs for their efficiency and consistency with priorities, adding: "At least to date, defendants have not offered any explanation for why a blanket suspension of all congressionally appropriated foreign aid, which set off a shockwave and upended reliance interests for thousands of agreements with businesses, nonprofits, and organizations around the country, was a rational precursor to reviewing programs."

a7471.speaker: Canal Holding, in partnership with Eutelsat and Strong
a7471.speech: Announce the official start-up of SeeAfrika, the first pan-African package, to create and maintain links between Africans on the continent and those of the diaspora.

a7471.speaker: Jean Jacques Silberstein, deputy managing director of Canal 3 Monde
a7471.speech: Indicates that the launch is the culmination of two years of work in France, Benin, the United States and Niger, and that the philosophy underlying the initiative is to deliver a satellite package destined for Africa from Africa ; “These are insurmountable difficulties that we are in the process of surmounting: a real challenge through a diversified, family-oriented and complete offering” ; says the package was designed to offer attractive, complete and rich content to the whole African family, where quality and beauty come first ; says that apart from international football, the programmes will really start between now and mid-March simultaneously in Benin, Niger and Burkina Faso.

a7471.speaker: Amandine Agonsanou, commercial manager of SeeAfrika
a7471.speech: Reported on the equipment and the various offers SeeAfrika is making available to the public: a Strong or Eutelsat dish of 60 or 80 cm and a subscription in two offers — the standard package with 10 channels plus 50 free channels for 2,500 CFA francs a month, and the full package with 16 international channels and 50 free channels for 9,500 CFA francs a month; to subscribe one need only go to a SeeAfrika showroom, buy a card and comply with the conditions available to the customer.

a7471.speaker: Abdourahamane Ousmane, chairman of the board of the Network of African Communication Regulatory Bodies (RIARC)
a7471.speech: Is proud to be present at the start of the activities launched Thursday 19 February, the concerns of RIARC — insufficient authentic audiovisual content produced by Africans for Africans, the low level of exchange of African content, the very low availability of African programmes, and the development of African media companies — being soon to be addressed.

a7471.speaker: Saadi Abdou, Niger's ambassador to Benin
a7471.speech: Says the partnership around SeeAfrika delights him and that the interest of the President of the Republic of Niger is justified by his commitment to development and to the reduction of poverty; SeeAfrika takes account of African realities and makes it possible to connect Africa with its diaspora.

a7471.speaker: Jean Gbeto Dansou, Minister of Communication of Benin
a7471.speech: Has very good impressions and thinks that SeeAfrika offers the possibility of following the news in all its forms and that this is a leap forward for the country.
